PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the petitioner is seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. There is no dispute as to the accident that took place on 30.09.2014 at about 9.15 p.m., on Manganahosahalli-Buddegudda road, Kikkeri Hobli, K.R.Pet Taluk, Mandya District, wherein a Tractor-Trailor bearing Reg.No.KA-06/TA-2462-63 hit against the motor cycle of the petitioner bearing Reg.No.KA-14/J-33, due to which, the petitioner sustained fracture of both bones of right leg, fracture of left clavicle.
He was treated at Government Hospital, K.R.Pet, Chamarajenda Hospital, NC: 2024:KHC:32935 Hassan under hospitalization between 01.10.2014 and 24.10.2014.
His claim for compensation of Rs.6 lakhs was opposed by the Insurance Company.
After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment awarded compensation of Rs.84,525/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
The Insurance Company has satisfied the award.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.M.Prakasha, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Krishna Kishore, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner was 45 years old,
Tractor driver, he was earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month, but the Tribunal assessed only at Rs.6,000/-.
The medical evidence is placed through Dr.Poornachandra that the petitioner has suffered limb disability of 34% whereas, the Tribunal taken disability only at 5%.
The compensation awarded towards pain NC: 2024:KHC:32935 and suffering, incidental expenses is on the lower side.
No compensation is awarded towards loss of amenities and discomfort and sought for enhancement.

sentences.text: Per contra, the learned Counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the Tribunal considered the avocation of the petitioner and also the medical evidence, correctly assessed the disability at 5%, in the absence of proof of evidence taken notional income at Rs.6,000/- and proportionately assessed the compensation.
He is fair enough to submit that nominal compensation may be awarded towards loss of amenities and discomfort and he has supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8. The medical records clearly shows the fractures suffered by the petitioner to his both bones of right leg and left clavicle.

CW-1/Dr.Poornachandra, Orthopedic NC: 2024:KHC:32935 Surgeon of Government Hospital, Hassan assessed the limb disability of 28% to the lower limb, 6% to upper limb, the Tribunal takes it at 5% to whole body.
Having regard to the petitioner being a Tractor driver aged 45 years, it is proper to assess the functional disability at 10% instead of 5% assessed by the Tribunal.

In the year 2014, a person with no proof of income will earn not less than Rs.8,500/-
and notional income of the petitioner has to be taken at Rs.8,500/-.
The medical bills produced for a sum of Rs.7,125/- is reimbursed by the Tribunal.
Compensation awarded by the Tribunal comparatively is on the lower side.
It is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.

SD/-
(T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA) JUDGE KNM Sri Venkatesha vs Sri Revanna on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82176989/
